evaluator: blind Phase 2 evaluator (independent inspection of artifact/, dist/ served locally, candidate suite plus independent probe tests)
summary: An honest, genuinely working Phase 2. Grand/Upright/Electric are real bundled recordings (packed PCM is byte-identical to the shipped WAVs, three clearly different harmonic profiles, MIT/CC0 provenance, fully offline: the served build fetches no sample files), Clav/Digital/Misc are oscillator-only synthesis and are declared as such, and the fallback path really is oscillator-only while reporting 'fallback' rather than 'ready'. I independently verified the signal graph: the destination has exactly one input (limiter <- master gain <- sum <- two layer levels), the documented unit order is physically wired, each of the six units plus Rotary measurably changes rendered audio, all-effects bypass returns a bit-identical dry signal, Reverb precedes Rotary, delay feedback filtering sits in the repeat path, and every Organ/Synth/Program control leaves rendered audio bit-identical. What holds the run back is panel feedback and layout. The six piano type LEDs are never synchronised (the typeLedValues helper is dead code), so after selecting Upright then Misc three type LEDs read 'on' at once while the engine plays Marimba; every effect type selector (Mod 1, Mod 2, Amp, Reverb, delay filter) changes audio with no visible or accessible indication of the chosen type; and in a real browser 55 of 162 controls are unclickable because the keybed overlaps the deck, with 7 controls rendering outside the chassis at 1440x900 and 107 outside it at 390x844. Tests are numerous and signal-based but run against a candidate-authored software DSP context rather than a real Web Audio backend.

evidence: Geometry measured in Chrome on the served build (artifact/dist): chassis 1354x451 at 1440x900 = 0.94 of viewport width (spec range 0.88-0.97), keybed 207px of 451px chassis height = 0.459 (spec 0.46), no page scroll.

Section widths measured as fractions of the chassis: performance 0.137, organ 0.195, piano 0.083, program 0.122, synth 0.244, effects 0.195 against specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json 0.14/0.20/0.085/0.125/0.25/0.20 - closely faithful and unchanged from Phase 1.

Keybed correct for the variant: 73 keys, 43 white / 30 black, E1-E7 (src/model/variant.ts, src/model/keys.ts); exactly two OLEDs (program-oled, synth-oled) and no OLED in performance/organ/piano/effects (src/components/sections.tsx).

Overflow is a real defect: at 1440x900 seven controls (piano-soft-release, piano-string-res, piano-sustped, piano-pstick, reverb-bright, reverb-global, rotary-on) render outside the .chassis rectangle; evidence/stage2-desktop.png shows FX legends clipped at the right edge ('ROTA', truncated REVERB rows).

At 390x844 the deck collapses to 122px tall and 107 of 162 controls fall outside the chassis bounds; evidence/stage2-narrow.png shows Piano/Program/FX content spilling over the keybed. The candidate's own regression.chassis test cannot catch this because it runs in jsdom, where all rects are zero (src/regression-chassis.test.tsx).

Presentation is a schematic labelled panel rather than a photogrammetric trace of nord-stage-4-73.jpg; the visual audit admits this (evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md 'Known deviations'). Materials are plausible (red chassis, dark inset plates, wooden cheeks, LED ladders) but micro-detail and control shapes are generic.

Piano type LEDs never track canonical state: typeLedValues() in src/model/apply-control.ts:165 is never imported anywhere (verified by search), so LED values only change for the individual LED you press. In Chrome, selecting Upright then Misc left aria-pressed true on grand, upright and misc simultaneously while data-piano-type was 'misc' and the OLED read 'Marimba'. Cycling with the TYPE button (piano-type) advanced type to 'electric' with all six LEDs unchanged (grand still the only lit one).

Effect type selection has no panel or accessible readout. Pressing reverb-type twice left the effects section's text and every aria attribute identical (only reverb-type's own aria-pressed toggles), and the same holds for fx1-type, fx2-type, amp-type and delay-filter. Nothing on the surface reveals Chorus vs Flanger, Hall vs Spring, or that Amp type is 'To Rotary' - the one setting that reroutes the layer into the Rotary.

FX focus buttons are three independent toggles (fx-focus-a/b/c in src/model/controls.ts) that only write state.fxSectionFocus; resolveFx()/applyHardwareControl() ignore it, so edits always target the focused piano layer regardless of the focus LED shown.

Working feedback does exist: layer enable/focus/level with 8-rung LED ladders (src/components/widgets.tsx LedLadder), per-unit ON LEDs that match processing, Program OLED showing the model label plus focused layer and 'LOAD FAIL / fallback playable' on failure, a data-piano-type/data-piano-layer surface state, and an honest status line ('Organ, Synth, and Program stay decorative').

All controls expose accessible names, roles and values (role=slider with aria-valuenow/aria-valuetext, buttons with aria-pressed) and are keyboard operable, which is how I had to drive most Piano controls because the keybed covers them.

Recordings verified, not asserted: I decoded src/audio/recorded-pcm.json and compared it byte-for-byte against the shipped WAVs - public/samples/grand/60v1.wav, upright/60v0.wav and electric/60v1.wav all match the packed PCM with meanAbsDiff 0.00e+0 (mono 16-bit 22050 Hz).

Three audibly different instruments: normalised harmonic magnitudes at MIDI 60 are grand 1.00/0.45/0.10/0.07, upright 1.00/0.80/0.10/0.13, electric 1.00/0.55/0.35/0.03; cross-bank meanAbsDiff 0.094-0.137. Bank inventory: grand 17 roots (36-84, 1 velocity layer), upright 17 roots x 2 velocity layers (32 zones), electric 17 roots.
Offline and bundled: the served build issues only index.js and index.css requests (network log), because the PCM is inlined in the bundle; no sample fetch occurs at runtime.

Provenance is complete and redistributable: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json names FluidR3 GM acoustic_grand_piano (MIT), FreePats Upright piano KW (CC0) and FluidR3 GM electric_piano_1 (MIT) with root notes and velocity layers, public/samples/LICENSES.md and MANIFEST.json enumerate every file, and scripts/pack-samples.mjs is the reproducible fetch/convert/pack pipeline.

Honest synthesis for the rest, verified structurally: with type clav/digital/misc a note creates oscillator nodes and zero AudioBufferSourceNodes; with grand/upright/electric it creates buffer sources (probe over the live node graph). In Chrome a Misc note started 2 oscillators and 0 buffer sources.

Sample-quality gaps against specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json 'sampleQuality': every zone is truncated to 0.71-0.78 s at 22.05 kHz and then looped (loopStart 0.14, src/audio/piano-engine.ts:370), so held notes are a looping decay tail rather than a natural one; roots stop at MIDI 36-84 while the keybed spans 28-100, so the top notes are pitch-shifted more than an octave from the nearest root (pickZone playbackRate = 2^((midi-root)/12)); grand and electric have a single velocity layer.
The piano-model encoder writes layers[focus].model (src/model/apply-control.ts:92) but no code ever reads it and the OLED shows only the type label, so the model dial selects nothing.

Both layers are real, separate signal paths: setupGraph creates createLayerGraph twice and connects each layer's level node into the master sum (src/audio/piano-engine.ts:258-268); my graph walk confirmed the master sum has exactly two inputs.

Enable/focus/level/octave all functional through applyHardwareControl (piano-layer-a/b-enable, -focus, -level, piano-oct-up/down), and layer focus also drives FX editing and the Program OLED - verified in Chrome: enabling and focusing layer B changed data-piano-layer to B and the OLED to 'Concert Grand / Layer B'.
Voice ownership verified: with both layers enabled a single note yields getLayerVoiceCount('A') > 0 and ('B') > 0 (src/piano-layers.test.ts), and enabling B raises rendered RMS by more than 1.15x.

Cleanup verified independently: after allNotesOff the active voice count returns to 0 and a walk from the destination no longer reaches any buffer-source node, so per-voice nodes are disconnected rather than left attached.
Octave shift is a single +/-12 step clamped at one octave (bumpOctave), which satisfies the spec's +/-12 semitones but offers no intermediate positions.

Every required detail control measurably moves rendered audio with directional assertions in src/piano-velocity-controls.test.ts: Light vs Heavy KB Touch RMS ratio > 1.15, Dyn Comp 3 raises a soft stroke > 1.2x, Timbre Soft vs Bright meanAbsDiff > 0.001, Unison 3 vs Off > 0.001, Soft Release lengthens the tail > 1.05x at 0.4 s, String Res changes the signal, Master Level 1.0 vs 0.15 RMS ratio > 1.5.

Implementations are real but simplified: KB Touch and Dyn Comp reshape velocity (shapedVelocity), Timbre only scales one lowpass cutoff (timbreCutoff), Unison adds detuned copies without stereo placement (unisonDetunes returns cents only), String Res adds three fixed partials to the struck note when the pedal is down or other notes are held (addStringRes) rather than resonating other strings, Soft Release multiplies release by 1.85 and is bypassed for Clav.

One behaviour contradicts the spec: Timbre 'Mid' multiplies the cutoff by 0.85 (src/audio/piano-engine.ts:490), i.e. it darkens, whereas specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json says Mid 'emphasizes midrange presence'. Dyno 1/2 are just brighter cutoffs, not preamp/EQ emulations.
Panel agreement holds for these controls (knob aria-valuetext and rotation follow the value, and the values feed the canonical state), unlike the type/LED problems noted above.
Sustain with damper cutoff works per layer; soft and sostenuto pedals are optional in the spec and are not claimed anywhere.

All four input paths exercised. Real Chrome: a mouse press on C4 started one AudioBufferSourceNode and set aria-pressed; holding computer keys z and x raised the count to 3 and marked C3/D3 pressed; releasing cleared them. jsdom tests cover independent multi-touch pointers, key-repeat suppression, MIDI note/velocity/CC64 and denied/disconnected MIDI (src/piano-inputs.test.tsx, src/interaction.test.tsx).
Sustain works from the UI pedal, Space and MIDI CC64 and honours per-layer SUSTPED: src/piano-pedals.test.tsx measures RMS at 0.4 s more than 1.3x higher with SUSTPED on and a later lastAudibleIndex.

Cleanup on focus loss verified in Chrome: dispatching window blur while a keyboard note was held cleared every pressed key; the provider also handles pagehide and visibilitychange, and MIDI denial/disconnect triggers allNotesOff (src/state/instrument-context.tsx).
Stress: my probe pressed 60 simultaneous notes and the voice count stayed at the 32-voice cap with deterministic oldest-first stealing, returning to 0 after allNotesOff.

Fallback is truthful: with failSamples the engine reports 'fallback' (never 'ready'), the detail string says 'labeled fallback', the type LED flashes and the Program OLED shows LOAD FAIL; I confirmed the fallback voice creates oscillators only and renders audible signal.

Minor real-browser wart: because init() awaits ctx.resume(), which does not settle before a user gesture in Chrome, the status line sits on 'Initializing audio' (data-audio-status=loading) until the first interaction, then flips to 'Audio ready - Grand/Upright/Electric recorded libraries loaded'.

One context, one destination, verified by walking the live node graph: destination has exactly 1 input, a DynamicsCompressor limiter, whose single input is the master gain, whose single input is a sum gain fed by exactly the two layer level nodes. Nothing bypasses the master path.

Ordered chain physically wired per layer (createLayerGraph in src/audio/effects.ts:454): input -> Mod1 -> Mod2 -> Delay -> Amp/EQ -> Comp -> Reverb -> fxBus -> (rotarySend | local) -> level, matching specs/nord-stage-4.effects.json requiredOrder. My graph dump shows the voice buffer source feeding that chain through to the limiter.
Master limiter configured with threshold -8 dB, ratio 20, attack 2 ms (createMaster), and Master Level ramps the master gain (applyState).
Parameter changes use short linear ramps (rampTo, 12 ms) and the all-bypass path crossfades a dedicated dry gain, so bypass produced a bit-identical dry render rather than a click.

Cleanup: dispose() stops all LFO oscillators and the rotary LFOs and closes the context; voice nodes are stopped and disconnected on release (verified: the destination chain no longer reaches buffer nodes after allNotesOff).

Two deviations. The spec says one Rotary instance per program, but createRotary is called inside each layer graph, so two rotaries exist (the audit admits 'Rotary is inserted per piano layer'). And an extreme worst case (8-note chord, both layers, unison 3, all levels max) still clipped 67 of 22050 samples at exactly 1.0, so the limiter reduces but does not fully prevent clipping.

I independently rendered each unit on versus a plain note (meanAbsDiff): Mod 1 0.0033, Mod 2 0.0141, Delay 0.0083, Amp 0.0975, Compressor 0.0006, Reverb 0.0208, Rotary 0.1509 - every unit processes real audio, and each unit's own On flag also changes the render.

Type-level distinctness is asserted pairwise in src/effects-processing.test.ts for all six Mod 1 types, all six Mod 2 types, all seven Amp/EQ types and all six Reverb types, with per-type non-silence checks; I re-ran the suite (41 tests, 16 files, all passing) plus my own 13 probe tests.

Implementations are recognisable rather than exemplary: Mod 1 has real LFO panning, tremolo, envelope-follower wah (waveshaper abs -> lowpass -> filter frequency) and LFO wah; Mod 2 has modulated delay lines and cascaded allpass stages for Chorus/Flanger/Phaser/Vibe/Ensemble/Spin; Amp/EQ is a lowshelf 100 Hz / peaking 200-8000 Hz / highshelf 4 kHz stack into a tanh drive curve with per-amp voicings and resonant LP24/HP24 modes; Reverb is a four-tap feedback loop with per-type delay times and decays.

Fidelity caveats: 'Ring Mod' modulates a gain around a positive offset (amplitude modulation, not true four-quadrant ring modulation); the reverb is a small feedback comb network with no diffusion, so Spring is distinguished only by a bandpass tone stage; amp models are documented tone approximations, which the spec allows as long as they differ - they do.

Per-unit bypass and all-effects bypass both real: with fxSectionOn false the render was bit-identical to a plain note for every unit configuration I tried (diff 0.00000), and toggling each unit's own On flag changed the render.
Dry/wet works: reverb mix 0.95 vs 0.15 and delay mix changes both alter the signal (src/effects-processing.test.ts), and applyDelay/applyReverb crossfade explicit dry and wet gains.
Delay feedback filter is in the repeat path, not the dry path: input -> delay -> filter -> fb -> delay with filter -> wet (createDelayUnit), and LP vs HP renders differ in the tail after 0.22 s.

To Rotary and ordering verified: setting Amp type 'To Rotary' with rotaryOn routes the post-reverb bus into the rotary (rotarySend up, local down), and I confirmed reverb precedes rotary by rendering routed-with-reverb vs routed-without (meanAbsDiff 0.0004+).

Group and global targeting are implemented: pianoGroup makes both layers read layer A's chain (resolveFx) and copies edits A->B; delay/comp/reverb global modes are settable both from dedicated global buttons and Shift+On (hardware['program-shift']).

Gaps: the manual Organ/Piano/Synth focus buttons do not retarget anything (fxSectionFocus is written but never read by resolveFx or applyHardwareControl) and are non-exclusive; delay tap tempo writes engine.state.layers[*].fx.delayTempo directly (PianoEngine.tapTempo), so the panel delay-tempo knob and React state diverge from the audio after a tap.

Audio responds immediately and coherently: type changes swap the source (Misc note -> oscillators only, Grand -> buffer source) and update the Program OLED in the same interaction; layer enable/focus/level, Master Level and every effect toggle take effect on the next note with ramped parameters.

But visible state contradicts or omits the selection in the two most important places. Three piano type LEDs read 'on' at once after two selections while the engine played a third type. Effect type cycling (Mod 1/Mod 2/Amp/Reverb/delay filter) leaves the panel textually and semantically unchanged, so the sound changes with nothing on the surface to say what was selected - including 'To Rotary', which silently reroutes the layer.

Positive feedback that does work: LED ladders track fader values, per-unit ON LEDs match processing, the Program OLED shows the model label plus focused layer, the type LED flashes and the OLED reports LOAD FAIL in the fallback state, and the status line reports audio status and MIDI state honestly.

Pointer feedback is additionally compromised because 55 of 162 controls (including the entire Piano type/detail cluster) sit under the keybed and cannot be clicked at all; they respond only to keyboard operation.

Denied/disconnected MIDI is handled: MidiController maps SecurityError/NotAllowedError to 'denied', the provider calls allNotesOff on denied/disconnected/unavailable, and src/piano-inputs.test.tsx drives a fake MIDI access through connect, note, CC64 and disconnect with the pressed key clearing afterwards.

Asset failure enters a labeled playable fallback: status 'fallback' (never 'ready'), oscillator-only voices (verified), flashing type LED and LOAD FAIL on the OLED; an audio-context construction failure yields status 'error' with a fallback message and keys that still track.
Rapid effect changes are safe: my probe applied six Mod 1 type changes at 20 ms intervals while a note sounded - no exception and output stayed well above silence.
Layered polyphony holds up: 60 simultaneous note-ons capped at 32 voices with oldest-first stealing and an 8 ms steal fade; voices and node connections returned to baseline afterwards.
No application console errors during a full real-browser pass (only a favicon 404 from my static server and the expected pre-gesture 'AudioContext was not allowed to start' warnings).
Clipping is not fully contained at extremes: 0.3% of samples pinned at full scale in the max-level layered unison chord render.

Clean boundaries: src/audio/types.ts defines injectable AudioContextLike/AudioParamLike interfaces, src/audio/software-context.ts supplies both the native-context factory and an offline software context, src/audio/effects.ts owns unit construction plus per-layer graph and master modules, src/audio/piano-engine.ts owns voices/status/state, src/model/* owns hardware definitions and canonical state, src/state/instrument-context.tsx wires inputs.

Platform boundaries are injectable end to end: createAudioContext and requestMIDIAccess are constructor/deps parameters (PianoEngineOptions, InstrumentDeps), so tests run without devices or audio output.

Reasonable Phase 3 headroom: LayerGraph exposes input/level/rotarySend plus a single apply(state, layer, time), and createMaster is separate, so more chains can be added. Two things would need generalisation first: LayerGraph.apply reads piano-specific state (layer.level gated on state.pianoOn) and each layer graph builds its own Rotary instead of sharing one.

State flow is single-source: applyHardwareControl produces the next InstrumentState from a control id plus value, and the provider pushes it into the engine; but it is a long flat if-chain (174 lines) and setInstrument is called inside the setValues updater, which is fragile under double-invoked updaters.

Volume and style are good: 16 files / 41 tests, all passing on a fresh install (pnpm run test, 8.8 s), deterministic, with rendered-signal assertions using tolerant relationships (rms, meanAbsDiff, lastAudibleIndex) rather than exact waveforms, and a complete tests/feature-matrix.json (20/20 required IDs mapped to non-empty files).

The important caveat: the 'real boundary' is the candidate's own DSP. renderPianoScript builds a SoftwareAudioContext (src/audio/software-context.ts, 713 lines of hand-written biquads, delay lines, compressor envelope and oscillators) and renders through it, so effect and instrument assertions prove the constructed graph against a self-authored simulator, never against an actual Web Audio/OfflineAudioContext implementation. I compensated by exercising the built app in Chrome, where the real path does work.

effects.graph coverage is thin for its weight: src/effects-graph.test.ts (19 lines) checks context identity, voice count and dispose only - nothing about the single destination, limiter, per-layer buses, node counts or ordered path. I had to write those assertions myself to confirm them.
src/piano-fallback.test.tsx claims the fallback stays playable but renders with a normal engine (renderPianoScript without failSamples), so it measures the sampled voice, not the fallback voice.

src/regression-chassis.test.tsx contains a tautology: expect(document.body.style.overflow === 'hidden' || ... || true).toBe(true), and all layout assertions run in jsdom where rects are zero - which is exactly why the real-browser overflow and hit-testing defects went unnoticed.

Code quality is decent: typecheck, oxlint, build and tests all pass cleanly on a fresh install; naming is consistent, files are small apart from the three audio modules, and control definitions/keys/state are normalised with stable IDs.

Load cost is heavy: dist is 11 MB, dominated by a 3.1 MB index js with the 2.8 MB base64 PCM inlined, plus a duplicate 2.9 MB recorded-pcm asset that the browser never requests (emitted only because of the Node-only new URL(...) reference) and 5.3 MB of public/samples WAVs that also go unused at runtime.

The artifact carries roughly 11.5 MB of stray build output: scripts/samples/_dl (9.9 MB of source mp3/flac downloads) and scripts/public/samples (1.6 MB of duplicated WAVs written from the wrong cwd).
Dead code: typeLedValues (which would have fixed the LED incoherence), loadRecordedBanks (the async fetch fallback is never called), and the layer 'model' field that nothing reads.

Runtime stability is otherwise fine: no leaked voices or nodes after cleanup, ramped parameter changes, per-note timers cleared through killVoice, and no console errors during repeated interaction; the provider does construct one PianoEngine in a useRef initializer and another in the mount effect, so an extra engine is created per mount.

issues: Piano type LEDs never reflect canonical state: typeLedValues (src/model/apply-control.ts:165) is dead code, so after selecting Upright then Misc the grand, upright and misc LEDs all read aria-pressed=true while the engine plays Marimba, and the TYPE cycle button advances the type with no LED change at all.

No panel or accessible indication of any effect type: cycling reverb-type, fx1-type, fx2-type, amp-type or delay-filter changes the audio while the effects section's text and aria attributes stay identical - including Amp 'To Rotary', which silently reroutes the layer into the Rotary.

55 of 162 controls cannot be clicked in a real browser at 1440x900 because the keybed overlaps the deck (document.elementFromPoint returns a key element at their centre), covering the whole Piano type/model/KB Touch/Dyn Comp/Timbre/Unison/octave cluster plus comp and delay/reverb switches; they are reachable only by keyboard.

Layout overflows the chassis: 7 controls render outside the chassis rectangle at 1440x900 and 107 of 162 at 390x844, with FX legends visibly clipped in evidence/stage2-desktop.png; the jsdom-only regression tests cannot detect this and one of them asserts a tautology (expect(... || true).toBe(true)).

Audio tests never cross a real Web Audio boundary: all rendered-signal assertions go through the candidate's own SoftwareAudioContext DSP, and effects.graph asserts nothing about the single destination, limiter or per-layer buses (I verified those independently).
Rotary is instantiated once per piano layer instead of the single shared instance the effects spec specifies, and the FX Organ/Piano/Synth focus buttons write state that no routing code reads.

Sample library is short and narrow: every zone is truncated to 0.71-0.78 s at 22.05 kHz and looped from 0.14 s, roots cover only MIDI 36-84 for a 28-100 keybed (top notes pitch-shifted more than an octave), and grand/electric ship one velocity layer, so uniform pitch-shifting is audible at the extremes.

Timbre 'Mid' lowers the filter cutoff (x0.85), the opposite of the spec's 'emphasizes midrange presence'; Unison is mono detune rather than detuned stereo voices; the piano-model dial changes state that nothing reads.
Delay tap tempo mutates engine state directly (PianoEngine.tapTempo), so the delay-tempo knob and React state no longer match the audio after a tap.

Artifact hygiene: ~11.5 MB of stray packer output committed under scripts/samples/_dl and scripts/public/samples, a 2.9 MB duplicate recorded-pcm asset emitted into dist that the browser never fetches, and dead code (typeLedValues, loadRecordedBanks).
Extreme worst-case load still clips: 8-note chord on both layers with unison 3 and all levels at maximum pinned 67 of 22050 samples at full scale through the master limiter.
In Chrome the status line stays on 'Initializing audio' until the first user gesture because init() awaits ctx.resume(), which does not settle before a gesture; it correctly reports ready afterwards.
